'''''Orixa japonica''''', commonly called '''East Asian orixa'''<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf|title=English Names for Korean Native Plants|publisher=[[Korea National Arboretum]]|year=2015|isbn=978-89-97450-98-5|location=Pocheon|pages=553|access-date=4 January 2017|via=[[Korea Forest Service]]|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170525105020/http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf|archivedate=25 May 2017}}</ref> or '''Japanese orixa''', is a deciduous shrub growing to {{convert|3|m|ft|sigfig=1}} with an equal spread.<ref>[http://www.canadaplants.ca/display.php?id=877 "Orixa japonica (Japanese Orixa)"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170105083253/http://www.canadaplants.ca/display.php?id=877 |date=5 January 2017 }} Canada Plants. Retrieved 8 September 2013.</ref> Native to China, Japan and South Korea, it is found on forested, sunny slopes at elevations from 500 to 1300 m.<ref>eFloras.org [http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=3&taxon_id=200012465 Chinese Plant Names, ''Orixa japonica'' Thunb.]</ref>
A recent scientific study found this plant to contain previously unknown alkaloids that may be effective against ''[[Plasmodium falciparum]]'', one of the protozoan species that cause human malaria.<ref name = Cirrus>Cirrus Digital: [http://www.cirrusimage.com/tree_Japanese_Orixa.htm Japanese Orixa ''Orixa japonica''] Retrieved 22 Feb. 2013</ref>

This plant has an unusual and distinctive leaf pattern. Starting from the oldest leaf, the [[Leaf angle distribution|pattern of angles of subsequent leaves]] is 180 degrees, 90 degrees, 180 degrees, and 270 degrees. The pattern then repeats.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/06/06/science/leaves-math-phyllotaxis.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201107230825/https://www.nytimes.com/2019/06/06/science/leaves-math-phyllotaxis.html |archive-date=2020-11-07 |first=Cara |last=Giaimo |title=Solving a Leafy Mathematical Mystery |website=[[New York Times]] |date=2019-06-06 }}</ref>
